notes:
Maintainer risk: HIGH — two spec-correctness bugs ship today that produce silently wrong wire requests (fetchHTMLBodyValues capitalization at JMAP-tjvm.3 + wrong 'using' capability set at JMAP-tjvm.4), and the extras-policy implementation diverges from the documented policy in two directions (clobber at .1/.2, silent-drop at .7). Each of these would generate a user issue with no obvious symptom — server returns empty htmlBody, or rejects the method, or loses vendor extras, with no error from the client. Canonical-template propagation amplifies every finding 7x across sibling extension-client crates.
Confidence: ~15% chance of missed bug.
Least confident flags:
  - JMAP-tjvm.5 (queryChanges filter/sort) — confident the spec REQUIRES filter+sort for correctness, but uncertain whether any production server in the wild actually enforces it. Stalwart in particular is lenient. The bug is real per RFC 8620 §5.6; the operational severity is server-dependent.
  - JMAP-tjvm.6 (search_snippet thread_ids) — confident the spec does not define threadIds for SearchSnippet/get, less confident about whether to remove the parameter or keep it as a documented vendor extension. Filed as a P0 to force the conversation, but the resolution is a design call.
Uncertainty driven by:
  - Did not exercise against a real JMAP server. All testing was wiremock + code reading + spec reading.
  - Did not test what serde_json does when a #[serde(flatten)] map contains a key that conflicts with a named field. Per the rule against probing without filing a bead first, the EmailImportInput per-entry extras clobber is left as a hypothesis under JMAP-tjvm.1/.2 sibling pattern, not a confirmed bug.
  - Did not audit jmap-base-client extract_response error handling, which sits downstream of every method here.
Would raise confidence if:
  - One round of real-server smoke (Stalwart in a container) confirming JMAP-tjvm.3 actually produces silent empty-htmlBody.
  - A second reviewer pass focused on the EmailImportInput per-entry extras clobber question.
API contract risk: MEDIUM — no single finding is a release blocker, but the cumulative shape of the API surface forces every caller into defensive boilerplate. The highest-value fixes are the typed filter/sort/create surface (JMAP-tjvm.18, .19, .20) and the missing #[non_exhaustive] on input params (JMAP-tjvm.16). Both are mechanical fixes that unlock safe spec-driven growth post-publish. The re-export coupling to jmap-types and jmap-base-client (JMAP-tjvm.17) is the single largest 1.0-stability hazard; the workspace's coordinated path-dep model masks it today but will bite hard at first publish. Documentation contract gaps (JMAP-tjvm.23, .26, .27, .28, .29) are low-individual-cost but high-aggregate-cost for callers writing production error-handling. The sealed-trait fix (JMAP-tjvm.31) is cheap now, expensive later.
API contract confidence: ~25% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags:
  - JMAP-tjvm.18 (untyped create) — confident the asymmetry exists, less confident about the right fix. The view-type design (EmailCreate omitting server-set fields) is non-trivial and may produce a worse API than the current Value escape hatch. Filing as P2 forces the conversation; resolution is a design call.
  - JMAP-tjvm.19 (untyped filter/sort) — confident the typed filter/comparator types exist in jmap-mail-types and SHOULD be used. Less confident about whether the workspace's typed FilterCondition fully covers the spec's filter algebra including FilterOperator nesting. Did not exercise the typed-filter path against a real query.
  - JMAP-tjvm.30 (search_snippet account_id override) — confident the inconsistency is real, less confident about the original intent. Possible the override was deliberate to support a future multi-account SessionClient design. Filed as P2 to force the discussion.
Uncertainty driven by:
  - Did not exercise typed-filter construction against jmap-mail-types::EmailFilter. The recommendation to use it depends on that type's completeness; I read its existence but not its full surface.
  - Did not audit the seven sibling extension-client crates to confirm propagation impact. Some findings here may apply unchanged; others may already have been addressed in the canonical-template propagation. The cookie-cutter rule means most apply.
  - Did not test what jmap_base_client::JmapClient and Session's auto-trait inheritance actually surfaces today (Send + Sync assumed from common patterns; not verified).
Would raise confidence if:
  - One round of propagation impact audit across the six sibling extension-client crates (chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing).
  - Static assertion test added per JMAP-tjvm.25 to confirm Send + Sync today.
  - Round-trip serialize/deserialize of a typed-filter construction against a real Stalwart server to verify the workspace's typed filter shape is wire-correct.
